content:
docs#CofiniteTopology right now is a type synonym. This is incosistent with docs#DiscreteTopology and docs#IndiscreteTopology which are Prop valued classes. From my experience, Prop valued classes are also nicer to deal with in these cases.

If we really want to keep the type synonym as well, we could make another WithCofiniteTopology (we have this for discrete spaces).

Agreed. Whenever possible, make statements about the Prop-valued typeclass. However there can be cases when you will want the type synonym (e.g., within a proof). Note that we have both docs#DiscreteTopology and docs#WithDiscreteTopology
Why bother with WithDiscreteTopology? Why do we not just write WithTopology X ⊥, as it's shorter? Is it just so that naming reflects the discreteness?
I think it is important to have WithDiscreteTopology for readability.
I agree, it's also not super clear if WithTopology X ⊥ means the discrete or indiscrete topology, if one isn't too familiar with that hierachy
It would be great if ⊥ could pull its infoview hover from the docstring for the corresponding Bot instance
Though I guess that wouldn't help in the source
Could one unexpand \bot or \top to Discrete and Indiscrete in the context of the order of topologies?
(see also #mathlib4 > completeGraph vs ⊤ @ 💬 in which a similar discussion happened around SimpleGraph)
